'''Chandrashekhar B. Khare''', {{post-nominals|FRS}} (born 1968) is a professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of California Los Angeles]]. In 2005, he made a major advance in the field of [[Galois representations]] and [[number theory]] by proving the level 1 [[Serre conjecture (number theory)|Serre conjecture]],<ref>{{Citation |last=Khare |first=Chandrashekhar |title=Serre's modularity conjecture: The level one case |year=2006 |journal=Duke Mathematical Journal |volume=134 |issue=3 |pages=557–589 |doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-06-13434-8 }}.</ref> and later a proof of the full conjecture with [[Jean-Pierre Wintenberger]]. He has been on the Mathematical Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] from 2015, serving as Jury Chair from 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Infosys Prize - Jury 2020|url=http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/prize/jury/jury-2020.asp|access-date=2020-12-10|website=infosys-science-foundation.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Resident of [[Mumbai]], India and completed his undergraduate education at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]]. He finished his thesis in 1995 under the supervision of [[Haruzo Hida]] at [[California Institute of Technology]]. His Ph.D. thesis was published in the  ''[[Duke Mathematical Journal]]''. He proved [[Serre's modularity conjecture]] with [[Jean-Pierre Wintenberger]], published in ''[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]''.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Khare |first1=Chandrashekhar |last2=Wintenberger |first2=Jean-Pierre |year=2009 |title=Serre's modularity conjecture (I) |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |volume=178 |issue=3 |pages=485–504 |doi=10.1007/s00222-009-0205-7 |bibcode=2009InMat.178..485K |s2cid=14846347 }} and {{Citation |last1=Khare |first1=Chandrashekhar |last2=Wintenberger |first2=Jean-Pierre |year=2009 |title=Serre's modularity conjecture (II) |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |volume=178 |issue=3 |pages=505–586 |doi=10.1007/s00222-009-0206-6 |bibcode=2009InMat.178..505K |s2cid=189820189 }}.</ref>

He started his career as a Fellow at [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]]. He was appointed as an associate professor of mathematics at the [[University of Utah]] until he moved to [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] in 2007. As of the year 2025, he is Professor and Chair of the [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] Department of Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UCLA Department of Mathematics |url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/people/ladder/shekhar |access-date=2025-05-23 |website=math.ucla.edu}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Khare is the winner of the INSA Young Scientist Award (1999),<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.org/youngmedal.php |title=INSA Young Scientist Award |access-date=20 August 2014 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131011230428/http://www.insaindia.org/youngmedal.php |archive-date=11 October 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Fermat Prize]] (2007), the [[Infosys Prize]] (2010),<ref>[http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/infosys-prize-2010-winners.html#mathematicalsciences Infosys Prize 2010 - Mathematical Sciences] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101117022339/http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/infosys-prize-2010-winners.html#mathematicalsciences |date=17 November 2010 }}</ref> and the [[Cole Prize]] (2011).

He gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited talk at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010, on the topic of "Number Theory".<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=15 August 2013|archive-date=8 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-27.</ref> and was elected as a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/six-scientists-of-indian-origin-elected-fellows-of-royal-society/article3342952.ece|author=Hasan Suroor|title=Six scientists of Indian origin elected Fellows of Royal Society|work=The Hindu|date=22 April 2012}}</ref>
